name: Delusion (moha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna declares his delusion gone through the supreme secret teaching called adhyātma (11.1); the Lord bids him not be bewildered (vimūḍhabhāva) at the terrible form (11.49); one who knows the Lord as unborn and beginningless is undeluded among mortals (10.3); freedom from delusion (asaṃmoha) is among the states that arise from him (10.4).
antidotes: Knowing the Lord as unborn, beginningless, great lord of the world (10.3)

name: Ignorance veiling knowledge (ajñāna)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The darkness born of ignorance, which the Lord, out of compassion for his devotees, destroys with the shining lamp of knowledge (10.11).
antidotes: The Lord's lamp of knowledge, given to those ever joined who worship him with love (10.10–11)

name: Fear (bhaya)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Fear and fearlessness are among the states that arise from the Lord (10.4); Arjuna and the worlds tremble at the terrible form (11.20, 11.23–25), he stammers in fear (11.35) and his manas is shaken with fear (11.45); the Lord bids him be free of fear (vyapetabhīḥ, 11.49); the devotee dear to the Lord is freed from fear (12.15).
antidotes: The Lord's resuming his gentle form and consoling (11.49–51)

name: Aversion (dveṣa)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The devotee dear to the Lord hates no being (adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānām, 12.13) and neither rejoices nor hates (12.17); 'without enmity toward any being' (nirvaira, 11.55).

name: The sense of 'mine' (mamatva)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Its absence (nirmama) is a mark of the devotee dear to the Lord (12.13).

name: The sense of 'I' (ahaṃkāra)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Its absence (nirahaṅkāra) is a mark of the devotee dear to the Lord (12.13).

name: Attachment (saṅga)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The one free of attachment (saṅgavarjita) who does the Lord's work comes to him (11.55); the devotee dear to him is free of attachment (saṅgavivarjita, 12.18).

name: Grief (śoka)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The devotee dear to the Lord does not grieve (na śocati, 12.17).

name: Attachment to the fruits of action; making the fruit one's motive (karmaphala-hetu)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: For one unable to do the higher practices, the relinquishment of the fruit of all actions is enjoined (12.11), and peace follows it immediately (12.12).

name: Heedlessness (pramāda)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna asks forgiveness for addressing the Lord rashly as a friend, not knowing his greatness, 'through heedlessness or through affection' (11.41–42).

name: Elation (harṣa)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The devotee dear to the Lord is freed from elation, impatience, fear and agitation (12.15) and does not rejoice (na hṛṣyati) (12.17).
notes: In 11.45 Arjuna reports being thrilled (hṛṣita) at the vision; the text does not call that a fault.

name: Impatience, intolerance (amarṣa)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The devotee dear to the Lord is freed from elation, impatience, fear and agitation (12.15).
notes: Commentators gloss amarṣa as intolerance or resentment (e.g. at another's gain); the verse gives only the word.

name: Agitation (udvega)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The devotee dear to the Lord is freed from agitation; the world does not shrink from him nor he from the world (na udvijate, 12.15).
